title: Detect stalled producers, end them early, and keep progress records
summary: The producer stage gets progress visibility. Periodic progress events (tool-call count and files changed) go to the job's records. A producer with no progress for a configured interval is killed early with a stall reason, and its partial workspace diff is kept. The audience is the maintainer diagnosing stuck jobs. A fake stalling producer test covers it.

defaults_applied.how: All code and the fake-producer test are Rust.
Add unit and integration tests; cargo test passes and clippy is clean.
Criteria check that a stalled fake producer is actually killed early with the reason and the diff is kept.
Stall detection is enforced in the driver loop, not described in prose.
Progress events and the kept diff go through the existing redactor.
One focused change; deadline-overrun recording is untouched.
The verifier runs cargo test on the stall test.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The driver loop in crates/athena-agent/src/claude.rs (1s recv_timeout, deadline check, kill_group) is where stall detection belongs. The UsageSink in crates/athena-core/src/invocation.rs is where progress is recorded.
Progress means a new tool call or a change in the workspace's changed-file set. A long-thinking producer is flagged only if it has issued no tool call and changed no file for the whole interval.
The stall interval is a new setting in athena.toml [agents], read through athena-data config, with a default well under the 1800s deadline.
A stalled kill is recorded as outcome Killed with a detail beginning 'stalled: no progress for Ns'. No new outcome enum value is added unless the record schema already needs one.
The partial workspace diff is saved to the job's records or state before the workspace is discarded, redacted like other agent text.
How deadline overruns are recorded is a separate queued item. This change leaves the existing deadline path and its wording unchanged.

acceptance_criteria.text: Run `cargo test` (workspace). A new test drives a fake producer that emits no progress with a short stall interval and a long deadline. It asserts the invocation ends as Killed well before the deadline, with a detail naming a stall and the interval, not 'deadline of'.

Run `cargo test`. A test with a fake producer that makes tool calls and edits files asserts that progress events are recorded in the job's records, each with a tool-call count and a files-changed count, and that this producer is not flagged as stalled.
Run `cargo test`. After the stalled kill, the partial workspace diff of the fake producer's edits is still present in the job's records or state, and a test reads it back.
A reader of the job's records can tell a stall kill from a deadline kill by the recorded reason alone. The deadline path and its message are unchanged.
The stall interval is a documented setting in athena.toml [agents] with a default, loaded via config. athena.toml is named here as a changed governance file.
Run `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check`. Both are clean.
CHANGELOG.md and the relevant doc (docs/architecture.md or docs/decisions.md) describe the progress events, the stall rule, and the diff retention.

out_of_scope: How deadline overruns are recorded (a separate queued item).
Changing the overall deadline or budget caps.
Stall detection for roles other than the producer, unless it falls out for free.
Retrying or resuming a stalled producer.
departures: The change touches the driver loop, the config, the records and a new test, so it is larger than the typical job. I raised cost and time slightly and lowered the pass probability.
